samples.summary: Blockquote task-click test uses a one-line fixture, so the source-line mapping it claims to check cannot fail
samples.evidence:
`it('toggles a task item inside a blockquote')` renders exactly `'> - [ ] quoted todo'` and asserts `toggles).toEqual([[0, true]])`. Line 0 is the only line in the document, so any mis-mapping of `list_item_open.map` inside a blockquote (the actual risk the test exists for) would still report 0 — the assertion holds regardless. The sibling non-quoted test (line 85) deliberately uses a multi-line fixture (`'# notes

- [ ] todo
- [x] done'`, indices 2 and 3) precisely to make the offset meaningful; the quoted variant should do the same, e.g. `'a

> - [ ] quoted todo'` expecting line 2.
searchedFor: grep for TASK_LINE_ATTR / note-task-source-line in preview.ts

samples.summary: New BARE_BOX_RE quote prefix is only tested for a single `> `; nested quotes and quote+indent go untested
samples.evidence: The regex was widened from `^(\s*)` to `^( {0,3}(?:> ?)*\s*)`, which admits repeated markers (`> > `, `>> `), a leading 0–3 space run before the quote, and indent after the quote. checkbox-input.test.ts adds exactly one case, `mount('> [ ]')` (line 62). No test covers `'> > [ ]'`, `'>> [ ]'`, `'  > [ ]'` or `'>   [ ]'` (whose `- ` must land after the quote at the line's own indent), nor a negative case for an unpeelable quote such as `'    > [ ]'` / `'\t> [ ]'` where the handler must not fire. A wrong prefix re-emission here silently rewrites the user's line.

samples.summary: quoteDepth / multi-level quote support in list-commands has no test above depth 1
samples.evidence: `quoteDepth` counts `>` characters and `QUOTE_RE` is `/^ {0,3}(?:> ?)+/`, i.e. the whole feature is defined for arbitrary nesting (`'> > '`, `'>> '`). Every new test in list-commands.test.ts (lines 40–94, 253–298) uses at most one `>`. Nothing exercises a depth-2 quote for indent/outdent (`'> > - a\n> > - b'`), for ordered-counter keying (a depth-1 and a depth-2 list in one selection must each start at 1), or for the `>>`-vs-`> >` equivalence the doc comment on quoteDepth explicitly claims. A depth-counting mistake would renumber or re-indent quoted lists wrongly with no failing test.

samples.summary: shift()'s depth filter is tested only in one direction (quoted line below an unquoted top line)
samples.evidence: `shift` now skips any selected line whose `quoteDepth` differs from the top list line's. The added test 'leaves a selected line in another blockquote where it is' (list-commands.test.ts:269) covers top=unquoted, other=quoted. The reverse — top line quoted, a following selected plain line (`'> - a\n> - b\n- c'`, select 2..3, indent) — is untested, as is the `if (!top) return;` early exit added at line 342/343. If the filter were inverted or the depth compared to the wrong line, an unquoted item would be shifted by a step measured inside a quote.

samples.summary: aria-label edge cases untested: empty item text (the `if (name)` guard) and the interactive (onToggleTask) mount
samples.evidence: `render` writes `aria-label` for every checkbox but only `if (name)`. preview.test.ts:64 covers only a read-only mount with two non-empty items. No test renders `'- [ ]  '` (empty task text, where no attribute must be written and no empty aria-label emitted) and none asserts the label is present when `onToggleTask` is supplied, although the doc comment at preview.ts:53-55 claims the name is announced 'either way'.

samples.summary: No test for a truly empty separator line between quoted items (depth 0 vs 1) ending the itemAbove walk
samples.evidence: The added test 'nests across the blank separator of a loose quoted list' (list-commands.test.ts:281) covers the bare `>` separator (same depth). The complementary case, `'> - a\n\n> - b'`, where the empty line has depth 0 and so terminates `itemAbove`/`parentOf` (canIndent false — arguably the intended markdown reading, since an empty line closes the blockquote), is not asserted anywhere, so a change to that boundary would go unnoticed.
